title: Customer security evidence orchestration and priority lanes
creator: Aisha Chen
description:
Problem: Enterprise sales and CS teams are receiving repeated asks for security evidence (SOC2 reports, DPA clarifications, HIPAA controls, vendor questionnaires). Current handling is ad-hoc, often manual and high-effort for low-risk asks, causing slow response times for customers and blocking deals.

Goal: Design a prioritized, low-touch orchestration layer that routes incoming security/compliance requests into one of three lanes: self-serve evidence, delegated response (templated answers + reviewer), and high-touch legal/security handling. The solution should reduce median time-to-first-response for low/medium risk asks to <24 hours, cut manual work per request by 60% for templated questionnaires, and provide audit trails and SLAs for high-touch lanes.

Scope: Intake routing and prioritization rules, canonical evidence bundle (auto-assembled), templated responses for common questionnaire items (GDPR, SOC2, DPA), lightweight reviewer workflow (security/PD/Legal), and metrics/dashboard. Interface changes are limited to console intake form + CS playbook integrations (Zendesk/Drive links).

Acceptance criteria: 
- Defined prioritization rules with risk signals (customer tier, contract type, data residency, request type).
- Endpoint that generates a canonical evidence bundle for common asks (SOC2 summary, encryption details, data residency statement).
- Library of 50 templated questionnaire answers covering top vendor questionnaires mapped to product controls.
- Routing automation that places ~70% of incoming requests into self-serve or delegated lanes.
- Dashboards showing response SLA, lane distribution, and time saved.

Proposal:
1) Intake schema: require structured fields (customer name, tier, region, ask type, urgency, form link). Add optional file upload for questionnaires.
2) Signal-based scorer: lightweight rule engine (tier priority, legal region, data type flagged HIPAA/GDPR, contract exists, previous denial history) producing scores: low/med/high.
3) Evidence assembler: map catalog of artifacts to request types and assemble a zip containing current SOC2 attest, encryption summary, DPA excerpt, deployment model description, and contact owner. Maintain artifact canonical IDs in a Google Drive folder with versioning.
4) Template responder: UI for CS to send templated answers with placeholders; templates require reviewer if they touch contractual exceptions.
5) Audit + SLA: log all actions to internal audit log and show per-request SLA in console.

Trade-offs and open decisions:
- Rule engine: start rule-first (fast) vs ML classifier (accurate). Proposal: rule-first with telemetry to collect training data for later ML.
- Evidence storage: store canonical artifacts in Drive vs in Redwood private object store. Start Drive for speed, roadmap to private store behind access controls.
- Template coverage: aim for 50 high-leverage templates first, expand iteratively.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1 (Design): finalize intake schema, prioritization rules, and template list.
- Week 2 (Build): implement intake form + builder for evidence assembler and templates.
- Week 3 (Pilot): enable with two CS reps and one AE team, collect feedback.
- Week 4 (Ramp): expand to full CS/Legal flows, launch dashboard.

Metrics: "time_to_first_response", "requests_by_lane", "manual_hours_saved_estimate", "templates_used", "SLA_violations".

Stakeholders: Product (Aisha Chen), CS (Priya Nair), Sales Ops (Jon Park), Security (Diego Morales), Legal (Mariana Silva), Eng runtime (ENG-1842 lead), DX (design collaboration).

Links: canonical questionnaire inventory (https://drive.google.com/drive/fake-inventory), initial template doc (https://docs.google.com/document/fake-templates), mock intake form Figma (https://www.figma.com/file/fake-intake), related PRD (confluence: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SEC/pages/12345).
updates: 2025-03-06 - Aisha Chen: Kickoff meeting with CS and Security. Agreed prioritization signals: customer_tier, contract_signed, data_type, country. Decision to prototype rule-based scorer first.

2025-03-07 - Diego Morales: Security input: HIPAA-labeled requests must go to high-touch unless customer is SMB and only requesting certification copy. Shared list of control excerpts for evidence bundle.
2025-03-09 - Priya Nair: CS pilot volunteers assigned (2 reps). Provided sample Zendesk flow and 18 recent requests exported for template mapping.
2025-03-11 - Eng(ENG-1842) review: Prefers storing canonical artifacts in Drive for MVP; flagged auth and rotation requirements. Estimated 3 stories to implement assembler API.
2025-03-12 - Aisha Chen: Updated acceptance criteria to include 50 templates and target 70% automation. Added due_date for pilot completion.
review_feedback: 2025-03-08 - Mariana Silva (Legal): Requested explicit gating for contractual exceptions; templates that affect contract terms must be flagged for Legal review.
2025-03-10 - Jon Park (Sales Ops): Suggested adding "deal_stage" as a signal to prioritize asks for late-stage opportunities.
2025-03-11 - UX: Recommended inline help and canned responses be editable by CS without code changes.

Create 50 initial templates and map to questionnaire items
Implement rule-based scorer and integrate with Zendesk webhook
Build evidence assembler that zips canonical artifacts and returns a secure link
Pilot with CS reps and measure metrics for two weeks
